verdict: LyondellBasell swung from a $890M loss a year ago to a $758M profit as last year's $1.2B of impairments did not repeat and Intermediates & Derivatives earnings surged.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: sales & other operating revenues, vs a year ago

segments.name: Olefins & Polyolefins – Americas
segments.note: Olefins, polyethylene and polypropylene sold to customers in the Americas (intersegment sales excluded, so the five customer lines foot to total revenue).

segments.name: Olefins & Polyolefins – EAI
segments.note: The same chemicals sold to customers in Europe, Asia and internationally.

segments.name: Intermediates & Derivatives
segments.note: Propylene oxide and derivatives, oxyfuels and intermediate chemicals such as styrene and acetyls — the largest customer line this quarter, helped by strong oxyfuels.

segments.name: Advanced Polymer Solutions
segments.note: Compounding and solutions: polypropylene compounds, engineered plastics, masterbatches and colors.

segments.name: Technology
segments.note: Licensing chemical and polyolefin process technologies and selling catalysts.

takeaways.title: The swing is mostly last year's pain
takeaways.text: A year ago the quarter absorbed $972M of goodwill impairments and $230M of other impairments on the way to a $890M loss. With no impairments this quarter, net income was a $758M profit on revenue up 10% to $8,499M.

takeaways.title: Intermediates led the segments
takeaways.text: Intermediates & Derivatives EBITDA was $720M (before identified items $795M), ahead of O&P–Americas at $641M, as oxyfuels strength and higher profitability offset softer O&P–Americas polymer and olefin prices versus last quarter.

takeaways.title: Clean earnings were $828M
takeaways.text: Excluding $70M of identified items net of tax ($0.22 per share) — mainly European propylene-oxide joint-venture closure costs — net income was $828M, or $2.54 per diluted share.

oneTimers: Identified items totaled $70M net of tax ($0.22 per share): pre-tax site closure costs of $77M (European propylene oxide joint venture), $2M of Cash Improvement Plan costs and a $9M European transaction credit, plus discontinued-operations effects. Excluding identified items, net income was $828M ($2.54 per share).
The year-ago quarter included $972M of goodwill impairments and $230M of other impairments, which is why the year-ago result was a $890M net loss.
otherDetail: Net other expense of $122M: interest expense $138M, partly offset by $29M of interest income, $3M of other income and $2M of equity-investment income — and including the $18M loss from discontinued operations (the former Houston refining business), net of tax, so the flow lands on total net income.
footerNote: LyondellBasell is a foreign issuer reporting in U.S. dollars; this quarter's release was furnished on Form 8-K with the full statements in the 10-Q (the task brief expected a 6-K — the company in fact filed an 8-K/10-Q this quarter). Segment revenue uses sales to external customers from the 10-Q, which foot to the $8,499M total; gross segment sales including intersegment transfers are higher. The $187M tax line is the continuing-operations provision; the discontinued-operations loss sits in Other expense as described, so the flow reconciles to total net income of $758M.
